entities.name: Al Azhar Al Sharif...
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Al-Azhar al-Sharif is the world's oldest continuously operating Islamic university and mosque complex, founded in 970-972 CE in Cairo by the Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah. For over a millennium, Al-Azhar has been the supreme authority on Sunni Islamic scholarship, issuing fatwas (religious legal opinions) that guide Muslim practice for approximately 1.8 billion Sunni Muslims worldwide.

Founded initially as a Shia Ismaili institution by the Fatimid dynasty, Al-Azhar transformed into Sunni Islam's leading institution after Saladin's conquest of Egypt in 1171 CE and his abolition of the Fatimid caliphate. The university's curriculum, combining Quran, hadith, jurisprudence (fiqh), Arabic grammar, and rhetoric, became the template for Islamic education worldwide. Al-Azhar graduates have established madrasas and Islamic institutions across Africa, Asia, and Southeast Asia.

Al-Azhar's relationship with Egyptian political power has been complex: under Nasser (1952-1970), the state nationalized Al-Azhar, bringing it under government control. Under President el-Sisi, Al-Azhar's Grand Sheikh Ahmed el-Tayeb has called for 'religious revolution' against extremist interpretations of Islam while resisting full state subordination. Al-Azhar's condemnation of ISIS as un-Islamic, its dialogue with Vatican Pope Francis (2019), and its opposition to child marriage and female genital mutilation represent its evolving role in 21st-century Islamic jurisprudence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Azhar's 1,050 years as Islam's supreme scholarly authority make it the most influential institution in the lives of 1.8 billion Sunni Muslims, shaping Islamic law, education, and religious practice across the world.
